messages.author: f45f3c6b0ac83795
messages.subject: Variogram interpretation/AKDE help
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am studying brood rearing ecology of geese but am struggling to fit a biologically logical home range estimate for half of them using the AKDE or wAKDE methods. When I look at the variograms, they appear to be very different for my data as compared to the samples we did during the workshop, as they seem to have stark temporal variation and not a set asymptote. I believe this lack of fit may be the root of my problem, but I am new to ctmm and spatial analysis in general so I would love some advice on how to proceed! I have already changed the time period I am using to limit natal dispersal (I found that on a different thread) and incorporated an error radius for each GPS transmitter to 10m. 

Here are the variograms with the ctmm.guess associated with them:



All of these variograms returned a HR estimate of over 1000km, which is highly unlikely for a gosling to be able to remotely cover. I feel like it may be an issue of bandwidth, but I'm not sure how to fix that. Do you have any advice?

Thanks
Mairin Murphy

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Variogram interpretation/AKDE help
parts:
Hi Mairin,

These variograms don't look range resident. At best, it looks like you might be able to segment some of these in to short range and long range behaviors. If they are brood rearing, have you tried segmenting out the nest? That's often necessary for CPFs.

Best,
Chris

Hey Chris,

Okay I fixed these! There were some illogical points that were throwing off the model, so I removed those and it worked well. Now I am having an issue calculating the speed of some of my birds. I segmented the time frame to when the transmitters were deployed to when the birds became resident to calculate the speed during brood dispersal, but I am getting this error for three of my birds: 

In speed.ctmm(FITspeed755) : Movement model is fractal.

I couldn't fit a meta analysis for these birds because of the differences in time lag between the transmitters (I had that same issue with the AKDE) but when I go to calculate the speed, this error is thrown for two of the birds. What is wrong with the data that it creates a fractal model?

Thanks
Mairin

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Variogram interpretation/AKDE help
parts:
Hi Mairin,

That isn't an error but a warning. If the data are too coarse, then you can't estimate speed (see the Noonan et al. reference from the help file), but:
  1. You may still be able to estimate diffusion rates (if you see them in the model-fit summary) and do meta-analysis on those.
  2. Sometimes you can't estimate speed because the location-error model is insufficient. There is a vignette and cited pre-print covering this.
Why would this have given you problems with AKDE meta-analysis?

Best,
Chris
